newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil rebound on local demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil rebound on local demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rebounded slightly late on Thursday after sharp falls throughout the week as regional demand and firmer prices in the west stemmed the latest slide, market sources said.
"The market is seeing some support at these levels from China," one trader said.

January gas oil swaps traded this morning at $30.00 and $29.85 a barrel, but picked up slightly later and was last quoted at $29.90/$30.00, brokers said. Last Friday, January paper traded at a five-year record of $33.07.
Traders Asian fundamentals remained bullish with strong buying still seen from North Asia for the winter as gas oil stocks in China were seen at a critical low.
Overnight January Brent crude on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) lost a massive $1.13 a barrel to close at $22.16 while January gas oil futures lost $9.50 a tonne to end at $205.00.

The market collapse was attributed to bearish stock data released by American Petroleum Institute (API) on Tuesday and the flow of Iraqi crude also on the same day ater a six-year absence, traders said.
API figures showed that crude oil stocks rose 324,000 barrels, distillates stocks climbed by over two million barrels and gasoline were up by almost six million barrels.
Jet fuel prices were unchanged from midday with January jet fuel/gas oil swap spread or regrade last quoted at $1.65/$1.90 a barrel, about 20 cents below Wednesday's indications.
Fuel oil, which withstood Wednesday's fall in other products, edged up from midday values with January swaps traded at $118.00 a tonne on expectations of continued support from a local trader.
January swaps was last quoted at $117.75/$118.50.
Naphtha was offered down in line with the weaker overnight crudes prices, brokers said. January swaps was offered at $23.30 a barrel compared to Wednesday's offer price of $24.20, one broker said.
January naphtha traded late Wednesday at $23.70 a barrel, they said.
